authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: No generic Thassa's Oracle / Underworld Breach conversion (decisions L46).
No Hela (future release, no exception; L45).

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Graveyard hate shuts off unearth and the backup reanimation.
Sedris costs six; slow without fast mana.
Unearthed creatures are exiled without rescue.

value.interaction: Force of Will, Fierce Guardianship, Mana Drain, Deadly Rollick, Feed the Swarm, Cyclonic Rift, Toxic Deluge.
value.mana: 31 lands, fast mana and Signets for a six-mana commander.
value.protection: Force of Will, Deflecting Swat, Lightning Greaves.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Sedris gives every creature card in the graveyard unearth, which makes the whole graveyard reusable.
accepted_role.honest_note: Commander-native. The one Spellbook combo (1409-3821, Deadeye Navigator + Peregrine Drake) doesn't need Sedris, but Sedris can unearth either half. The deck has backup reanimation (Reanimate, Animate Dead, Necromancy, Living Death) but is far weaker without him. There is no source blueprint file; the closeout and verification are the evidence. M1 review (sedris-01..06, all verified) confirms the unearth and rescue rules.
